title: Gesture inertia and bulk-resize flow with inline filter predicate builder
creator: Ava Martínez
description: Problem: Users expect fluid, tactile column resizing on large virtualized tables but current behavior is fiddly for multi-column adjustments and loses context when density changes. We also have fragmentation between filter UX (modal vs. inline) that forces context switching. Goal: Design a unified interaction for single-column and multi-column resize that supports gesture inertia, an explicit bulk-resize flow (multi-select columns), keyboard parity, and an inline predicate filter composer that surfaces when column header filters are invoked. This ticket covers the interaction spec, visual tokens, accessibility mapping, and high-fidelity prototypes for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Single-column drag supports smooth inertia physics with optional snap points (narrow, default, wide) and respects user motion-reduce preference.
Multi-column bulk-resize mode: user can Shift+drag or marquee-select contiguous columns to resize them proportionally or distribute extra width evenly.

Inline filter predicate builder opens anchored to the column header and supports single-field predicates, an add-condition flow, and applied filter chips visible in the header with remove/edit affordances.
Keyboard support: arrow keys adjust width (+/- 8px step), modifier for fine-grain (1px), and bulk-resize and inline-filter actions operable via keyboard and announced by screen readers.
Performance: interactions maintain 60fps on recommended setups; prototypes validated against virtualized sample of 20k rows and variable column count.
Design tokens and density presets documented and shipped as part of design-system-2026.03 release notes.
Engineering sign-off from ENG-28910 on feasibility and ENG-28976 on perf benchmarks.
design_notes: Prototypes: Figma frame 'Column-Flow-Prototype-v2' includes inertia simulation and bulk-resize overlay. Motion: implement a friction curve (exponential damping) with soft snap thresholds at 64px increments. Snapping is optional via user toggle in table settings. Bulk-resize: when multiple columns selected, show a braided overlay indicating distribution preview. User flows: (1) single drag: standard handle; (2) double-drag on handle toggles 'even-distribute' mode; (3) Shift+click selects contiguous header range; (4) Alt+drag performs proportional scaling by initial width ratio. Inline filter: clicking filter icon opens anchored popover with field dropdown + operator + value chip; hitting Enter applies and converts to header chip. Accessibility: header handle uses role='separator' with aria-orientation and aria-valuenow; live region announces start/end of resize and final width. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by turning off inertia and snap. Tokens: introduce --table-column-snap-steps and --table-resize-handle-hitbox (px) for consistency across breakpoints.
decisions: Use physics-based inertia for pointer interactions but disable for reduced-motion and keyboard paths.
Provide both proportional and even-distribute bulk modes; default to proportional to avoid unexpected layout collapse for mixed-width columns.
Inline filter builder prioritized over modal for faster contextual edits; modal remains available for advanced multi-column filter composition.
Telemetry: emit lightweight events for resize-start/resize-end with delta to help tune default snap points and detect abuse; opt-out flag available for customers with strict telemetry policies.
